chunks: From him, from Ayoub, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, who said:

Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding a house that belongs to a man in a city or a farm, and he passes by it, [what is the ruling]? He said: 'If it is among what he has dwelt in, he completes the prayer in it; and if it is among what he has not dwelt in, he should shorten [the prayer].'
ai.seo_question: When should a traveler perform full prayer versus shortened prayer at their own property?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Hadi (AS) clarifies the criterion for traveler status based on actual habitation rather than mere ownership, a key distinction in Shia fiqh for determining when to perform full (tamam) or shortened (qasr) prayers. It highlights the principle that the intent and history of residence in a specific location define the legal status of the traveler, ensuring that the concession of qasr is not forfeited by incidental ownership of unoccupied properties.
